# Metaplate v0.9.0

Metaplate 0.9.0 is the Cloudflare Workers release. The experimental `metaplate/takumi` entry renders cards on a Worker with Takumi's precompiled WebAssembly. For Next.js on Workers through OpenNext, the new `definePlate` lets pages import a plate's URL contract without its renderer, while the build prerenders the cards. `metaplate render` can now write the social tags into static HTML pages. `metaplate verify-page` can treat a staging site's robots block as expected. `fetchImageLoader` loads per-page images safely on any Fetch runtime. Two new render guards, `fontFallback` and `lineClamp`, catch text Satori draws in the wrong font or without the clamp you asked for.

> **Upgrade recommendation:** Recommended for everyone, and worth a look if you deploy to Cloudflare Workers or an edge runtime. There is no runtime migration. TypeScript code that switches exhaustively over `RenderGuardIssue["guard"]` needs `"fontFallback"` and `"lineClamp"` cases. Scripts that parse the text output of `verify-page` for robots lines should read its `--json` output instead.

## Why upgrade

- **Cards on Cloudflare Workers.** `metaplate/edge` cannot start on Workers. Satori's bundled HarfBuzz compiles its WebAssembly at run time, which Workers forbid. `metaplate/takumi` renders there through a precompiled module, with the same plate surface as `createEdgeOg`.
- **Safe remote images on edge runtimes.** `remoteImageLoader` needs Node's DNS and sockets, so edge plates had to hand-write their own `fetch`. `fetchImageLoader` brings the same allowlist, redirect, byte, and time limits to the Fetch API.
- **Next.js on Workers without drift.** Pages on a Worker must not import the renderer, so they rebuilt image metadata by hand and restated the plate's `imagePath`, version, and revision. `definePlate` is the plate's contract with no renderer attached. Pages and the build share it, so their URLs cannot drift apart.
- **Silent rendering mistakes are caught.** A typo in `fontFamily`, a weight the family lacks, or a `lineClamp` on a flex column used to render with no error. The `fontFallback` and `lineClamp` guards report them.

## Highlights

### Rendering on Cloudflare Workers (experimental)

- `createTakumiOg` from `metaplate/takumi` renders plates with Takumi (`takumi-js`, a new optional peer, `>=2.22.1 <3`). It supports variants, handlers, `fetchableFrom`, ETags, output encoders, `languageFonts`, and every render guard except `avoid`. Emoji come from the plate's own emoji loader and never from a CDN. Takumi itself fetches nothing: an image `src` or CSS `url()` that is not a `data:` URI fails the render before any request, so remote images go through `fetchImageLoader` with its allowlist. Fonts must be TrueType, OpenType, or WOFF2. See [Takumi](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/takumi.md).
- Takumi lays out like a browser in a few places where Satori does not. It defaults to `box-sizing: border-box`, keeps an image's width in a flex row, and fails on a truncated image instead of drawing part of it. The guide lists every difference and shows how to compare a plate with `compareImages` before switching.
- On the Workers Free plan, a warm render measured about 13 ms of CPU, against the documented [10 ms limit](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). Serve cards with long-lived `Cache-Control` and an ETag, put them behind the Cache API, or render at build time. The Paid plan fits uncached rendering easily. The entry is not hosted-certified: the evidence is a spike Worker in production and a test that bundles the entry with Wrangler's `workerd` conditions and checks that it carries Takumi's [WebAssembly module](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/webassembly/) and no Node built-ins.
- A new parity suite renders 16 plates through both `metaplate/node` and `metaplate/takumi` and holds each to its own pixel budget. A `takumi-js` or `satori` update that moves layout fails before it merges.

### Next.js on Cloudflare Workers, and static pages

- `definePlate` in the root `metaplate` entry returns a plate's URL and metadata contract (`alt`, `size`, `variants`, `imagePath`, `basePath`, `origin`, `version`, `revision`, `contentType`) with the plate's `metadata`, `signedMetadata`, `image`, `sitePath`, and `variant` members. It imports no renderer. Spread it into `createNodeOg`, `createEdgeOg`, `createTakumiOg`, `createSvgOg`, or `createNextOg` and add `fonts` and `component`. Both sides run the same metadata code, and a test compares them across 288 option combinations. A factory throws when the contract's `contentType` is not what it serves. See [A contract without a renderer](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/plate.md#a-contract-without-a-renderer).
- A new guide, [Next.js on Cloudflare Workers](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/cloudflare-next.md), covers the hybrid setup for [`@opennextjs/cloudflare`](https://opennext.js.org/cloudflare/get-started). Cards are rendered into `public/` before the build and served as [Workers static assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/). Pages import only the contract, and `verify-page` checks the result after deploying.
- A `metaplate render` page can name an `html` file and its page-level tags. The command then writes the plate's social `<meta>` tags between `<!-- metaplate:social -->` markers, or before `</head>` the first time. `og:image` carries the same `?v=` URL the render recorded. Re-running writes the same bytes, and a page is written atomically and only after all of its images succeed. Malformed markers, a missing `</head>`, or a hand-written `og:image` outside the block fail the run before anything renders. See [Writing tags into static HTML](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/render-cli.md#writing-tags-into-static-html).

### Staging checks with verify-page

- `metaplate verify-page` prints one robots.txt line per crawler, listing the page and image URLs it blocks. It used to print the same block up to once per target and image.
- `--expect-robots-block` (`expectRobotsBlock` in `verifyRemotePage`) is for sites that block crawlers on purpose. A block is reported as expected, and the run fails when a crawler can fetch the page. `--json` adds a `crawler` field to robots issues, a per-crawler `expectation`, and a `robots-not-blocked` issue code; no field is removed. See [Sites that block crawlers on purpose](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/verify-page.md#sites-that-block-crawlers-on-purpose).

### Remote images on Fetch runtimes

- `fetchImageLoader` in `metaplate/image` is `remoteImageLoader` built on the Fetch API, for Cloudflare Workers (with `metaplate/takumi`), Netlify Edge, Deno, and Vercel Edge. It keeps the required `origins` allowlist, the URL, scheme, credential, and port checks, redirects re-checked on every hop, a byte cap enforced from `Content-Length` and while streaming, one time budget, and the bounded cache. It reports the same `RemoteImageError` codes, which `metaplate/image` now also exports. Fetch runtimes hide DNS, so it refuses only hosts written as non-public IP addresses or `localhost` names, and the allowlist is the boundary. See [Edge runtimes](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/rendering.md#edge-runtimes).

### Reliability

- The `fontFallback` guard, for `createSvgOg`, `createNodeOg`, `createEdgeOg`, and `createTakumiOg`, reports each font request that no loaded face satisfies, as `missing: "family"` or `missing: "face"`, with the loaded faces listed. It follows inline styles down the tree, calls nested function components, and counts faces from `languageFonts` as loaded. Like every guard, it is off by default. See [Render guards](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/rendering.md#render-guards).
- The `lineClamp` guard reports a clamp or ellipsis that Satori ignores and draws in full: `lineClamp` on an element whose display is not `block`, `WebkitLineClamp` without `-webkit-box`, `textOverflow: "ellipsis"` without `overflow: "hidden"` and a non-wrapping `whiteSpace`, and a clamp whose text sits inside a child element. A test renders every case through Satori, so a Satori update that changes these rules fails it. On Takumi, which clamps more cases, the guard applies Satori's rules so a plate stays portable.
- The rendering guide said plates have no stylesheet. Custom properties declared in the plate resolve in every adapter, and `<style>` elements apply in `createSvgOg`, `createNodeOg`, and `createEdgeOg` on Satori 0.51.0 or later. Only the site's own CSS is out of reach. `createNextOg` is the exception, and tests now pin each behavior.

## Breaking changes

None at run time. Two changes may need attention:

- `RenderGuardName` gains `"fontFallback"` and `"lineClamp"`, and `RenderGuardIssue` gains a member for each. TypeScript code with an exhaustiveness check over `issue.guard` needs a case for each. Both guards are off by default.
- The text output of `metaplate verify-page` shows each robots.txt block once per crawler, with only the deciding rule. Scripts that parse those lines should read `--json`, which only gains fields. Its `RobotsIssueCode` type gains `"robots-not-blocked"`, so an exhaustive switch over issue codes needs a case for it.

The existing peer ranges are unchanged. See [Upgrading](https://github.com/freeknet/metaplate/blob/v0.9.0/docs/upgrading.md#breaking-changes-by-version).

## Install or upgrade

```sh
npm install metaplate@0.9.0
```

That single command still includes the framework-neutral SVG and PNG renderer: npm 7+ and pnpm 8+ install the `satori`, `@resvg/resvg-js`, and `react` peers. Yarn needs them added explicitly. Node.js 20 or newer is required. `takumi-js` is optional and is only needed for `metaplate/takumi`. Add it with `npm install takumi-js` when you use that entry.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes: lint, the duplication scan, workflow pin policy, dependency inventory and Socket disposition policy, deployment evidence policy, release-note validation, source and example type checks, the full test suite, the build, and the package dry run. `npm run check:package` installs the packed tarball into fresh consumers and builds and serves the Next.js, Astro, React Router, SvelteKit, Express, and edge fixtures from it.
- `metaplate/takumi` is tested on Node.js through Takumi's native addon on Linux, Windows, and macOS, and as a Workers bundle built with Wrangler's import conditions. The Takumi spike found Takumi's Wasm and native outputs pixel-identical on all 19 of its fixtures.
- **Socket baseline.** It is the Socket CLI deep score of the published `metaplate@0.8.4`, captured 2026-11-25. The package scores 80 overall, and its own alerts are `recentlyPublished` and `unpopularPackage` (medium) and `urlStrings` (low). Two high dependency alerts carry time-bounded dispositions that expire 2027-04-30. `string.prototype.codepointat`, under the Satori peer, carries over. `obfuscatedFile` on `caniuse-lite@1.0.30001828` is new and is reached only through the optional `next` peer and development tooling. A tarball diff shows it is that release's new packed data format, with no dynamic code, network, or filesystem access, and it was published with SLSA provenance. The `tslib` ownership alert no longer appears. There are no critical alerts. Because the baseline scores the published 0.8.4, it does not yet cover the new optional `takumi-js` peer (a native addon and a WebAssembly build, mostly from one maintainer). The 0.9.0 package's own score will.
- npm registry signature and SLSA provenance verification run after publication, against the published artifact.
